collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — GOOD, BAD AND ORDINARY DAYS (DAY-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Wonderful days, rotten days, mixed days and days when nothing much happens at all. Moods come without reasons, small things matter more than they should, and nobody has to end the day happier, wiser or more productive than they started it.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager had a brilliant idea at dawn and has completely forgotten it: try to remember, or let it go.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: At dawn, half awake, (subject) had a brilliant idea. A truly brilliant one. It was going to change everything. (subject.He/she) thought, "I'll remember that," and went back to sleep. It is now the middle of the morning, and (subject.he/she) cannot remember a single thing about it, except that it was brilliant and something to do with baskets. Or possibly fish.

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) spends the whole day trying. (subject.He/she) stares at baskets. (subject.He/she) stares at fish. (subject.He/she) tells (friend), who suggests it might have been "a basket for fish," which already exists. By evening, (subject) has given up. The idea is gone. (subject.He/she) mourns it briefly and goes to bed with a piece of charcoal next to the mat.

o2__fx.name: Outcome B
o2__fx.text: (subject) decides that if the idea was really that good, it'll come back. (subject.He/she) gets on with the day. That afternoon, mending a net, (subject.he/she) suddenly remembers. It was to put a little handle on the bottom of a basket so you can tip it out more easily. That's it. That's the brilliant idea. (subject) doesn't know whether to laugh or be disappointed. (subject.He/she) makes the handle anyway. It's quite good.
